learn.hook: Who decides which side of the road we drive on, or when schools open? Someone has to make and run the rules. That's governance!
points: Governance is the way decisions are made, rules are put in place and a country, state or town is run for the good of everyone.
A government is the group of people and bodies that do this work. It makes laws, collects taxes and provides services like schools, hospitals, roads and safety.
Government has three organs (branches). The legislature makes laws. The executive puts laws into action. The judiciary (the courts) settles disputes and checks that laws are followed fairly.
Keeping these three powers separate, so that each checks the others, is called the separation of powers. It prevents misuse of power.
In India, Parliament is the legislature at the national level, and the Supreme Court is the highest court.

example.q: A new law says everyone must wear a helmet on a two-wheeler. Which organ makes the law, which enforces it, and which decides a dispute about a fine?
steps: The legislature (lawmakers) passes the helmet law.
The executive, through the traffic police, makes sure people follow it.
If someone disagrees with a fine, the judiciary (a court) decides.
example.answer: Legislature makes it, executive enforces it, judiciary settles disputes.

learn.reallife: Traffic signals, school timings, vaccination drives and garbage collection are all examples of governance you see every day.

games.title: Which organ?
items: Debates and votes on a bill

quiz.q: What is governance?
options: The way decisions are made and a place is run for everyone
quiz.explain: Governance means making decisions and rules and running a country, state or town.
quiz.mistake: Thinks governance is only about one person giving orders

quiz.q: Which organ of government makes laws?
quiz.explain: The legislature, such as Parliament, debates and passes laws.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the roles of the three organs

quiz.q: Which organ of government puts laws into action?
quiz.explain: The executive runs the government and carries out the laws.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the lawmakers also carry out the laws

quiz.q: Which organ of government settles disputes?
quiz.explain: The judiciary, made up of courts, settles disputes and interprets laws.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the courts with the lawmakers

quiz.q: What is the highest court in India?
quiz.explain: The Supreme Court in New Delhi is the highest court of India.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the High Court is the highest

quiz.q: Why are the powers of government divided among three organs?
options: To make work slower on purpose
So that nobody has to work
So that no one organ can misuse power
quiz.explain: Separation of powers lets each organ check the others.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the purpose of separating powers

quiz.q: What is the legislature of India at the national level called?
quiz.explain: Parliament is India's national legislature; it has the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the legislature with courts or local bodies

quiz.q: Which of these is a service provided by government?
options: Selling toys in a private shop
Playing in a cricket match for fun
quiz.explain: Governments provide services like hospitals, schools, roads and safety.
quiz.mistake: Confuses private activities with government services

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'What does a government actually do? Is it just one big boss?'
teach.praise: Now I know! The legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out and the judiciary settles disputes. No single boss!
teach.nudge: What are the three organs of government, and what does each one do?

learn.hook: Who fixes a broken streetlight, who runs the state's buses and who prints our currency? Different levels of government!
points: India has government at three main levels: the national (Union or Central) level, the state level and the local level.
The Union government looks after matters for the whole country, such as defence, currency, railways and relations with other countries.
State governments look after matters within a state, such as police, state hospitals and farming.
Local governments look after a village, town or city: drinking water, streetlights, cleanliness and local roads. In villages these are panchayats; in towns and cities, municipal bodies.
Each level has its own work, so that decisions are taken close to the people they affect.

example.q: Who should repair a broken streetlight in your lane: the Union government, the state government or the local government?
steps: A streetlight affects only one lane or ward.
Matters like streetlights and local cleanliness are handled by local government.
So the panchayat or municipal body should fix it.

learn.reallife: You meet all three levels: your coins and train tickets come from the Union government, your state bus from the state government, and your street's garbage collection from the local body.

quiz.q: How many main levels of government are there in India?
quiz.explain: India has three main levels: Union, state and local.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the local level

quiz.q: Which level of government is responsible for the defence of the country?
quiz.explain: Defence affects the whole country, so the Union government handles it.
quiz.mistake: Thinks states handle defence

quiz.q: Which level would usually manage street cleaning in a town?
quiz.explain: Local bodies like municipalities handle cleanliness of towns and cities.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the national government does every job

quiz.q: Who prints and issues currency notes for the whole country?
quiz.explain: Currency is a national matter, handled at the Union level through the Reserve Bank of India.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each state has its own currency

quiz.q: Which level of government is a gram panchayat?
quiz.explain: A gram panchayat is the local government of a village.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise panchayats as local government

quiz.q: Why do we need local government as well as national government?
options: Local problems are best solved by people close to them
Local bodies make laws for the whole country
quiz.explain: People nearby understand local needs like water, roads and streetlights best.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one level can do everything well

quiz.q: Which matter is usually handled by a state government?
quiz.explain: Police and law and order inside a state are state matters.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Union and state matters

quiz.q: Relations with other countries are handled by which level?
quiz.explain: Dealing with other countries is a national matter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks states make their own foreign relations

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Is there just one government? Who fixes my street and who protects the whole country?'
teach.praise: Got it! There are three levels: Union for the whole country, state for each state, and local bodies for villages and towns!
teach.nudge: How many levels of government are there, and what are they?

learn.hook: In your class election, every student gets one vote. That's a mini democracy!
points: Democracy is a form of government in which people choose their leaders and have a say in how they are governed.
In India, people elect representatives who make decisions for them. This is called representative democracy.
Every Indian citizen aged 18 years or above can vote, whatever their religion, gender, caste, wealth or education. This is universal adult franchise.
Elections are held regularly. The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament and to state legislatures.
India has a long tradition of discussion and assemblies. Ancient republics (ganas or sanghas), such as the Vajji (Vrijji) confederacy with its capital at Vaishali, took decisions in assemblies.

example.q: Why is it fair that every adult gets exactly one vote, rich or poor?
steps: In a democracy, every person is equal.
If some people got more votes, their wishes would count more than others'.
One person, one vote gives everyone an equal say.
example.answer: Because all citizens are equal, so each has an equal say.

learn.reallife: On election day, adults in your family get a mark of indelible ink on a finger after voting. It shows they have voted.

games.title: Democracy facts
items: In India, citizens aged 18 and above can vote.
In a democracy, only rich people can vote.
Every adult citizen can vote, whatever their wealth.
The Election Commission of India conducts national elections.
It conducts elections to Parliament and state legislatures.
In a representative democracy, people elect leaders to decide for them.
Elected representatives work on behalf of the people.
Vaishali was a famous ancient republic.
It was the capital of the Vajji (Vrijji) confederacy.
In a democracy, leaders are chosen by one family forever.
In a democracy, leaders are chosen by the people through elections.

items.text: The minimum voting age in India is ___ years.
Choosing leaders by voting is called an ___.
Giving every adult the right to vote is called universal adult ___.
Ancient republics were called ganas or ___.

quiz.q: What is democracy?
options: Government in which people choose their leaders
quiz.explain: In a democracy, people elect leaders and have a say in decisions.
quiz.mistake: Confuses democracy with monarchy

quiz.q: What is the minimum age to vote in India?
quiz.explain: Indian citizens aged 18 years and above can vote.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the voting age with another age limit

quiz.q: What is universal adult franchise?
options: Every adult citizen has the right to vote
quiz.explain: Every citizen aged 18 or above can vote, without discrimination.
quiz.mistake: Thinks voting depends on wealth, gender or education

quiz.q: Which body conducts elections to Parliament in India?
quiz.explain: The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Parliament and state legislatures.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Election Commission with courts or banks

quiz.q: What is representative democracy?
options: Everyone votes on every single decision every day
People elect representatives who take decisions for them
quiz.explain: In a big country like India, elected representatives act on behalf of the people.
quiz.mistake: Thinks people vote directly on every law

quiz.q: Which ancient city was the capital of the Vajji (Vrijji) republic?
quiz.explain: Vaishali was the capital of the Vajji confederacy, an early republic.
quiz.mistake: Picks a Harappan city

quiz.q: Why are elections held regularly in a democracy?
options: So that people can keep or change their leaders
quiz.explain: Regular elections let people judge their representatives' work.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why leaders must face the people again

quiz.q: Why does every voter get only one vote?
options: All citizens are equal, so each has an equal say
quiz.explain: One person, one vote reflects the equality of all citizens.
quiz.mistake: Does not link one vote with equality

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'What is democracy? Who chooses the leaders?'
teach.praise: Hooray! In a democracy, citizens aged 18 and above vote in elections to choose their leaders. Everyone gets an equal say!
teach.nudge: Who chooses the leaders in a democracy, and how? Who is allowed to vote?
